name: io.pugi/pugi
title: Pugi
description: Your AI product team: build websites and web apps, design logos, check security, publish.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: Use this when the person asks about their Pugi plan, credit or what they spent today. Free and read-only.

tools.name: buy_credits_link
tools.description: Get a link to add credit.

amount_usd.description: How much credit to add. Rounded up to a pack of 5, 10, 25, 50 or 100 USD. Default 5.

tools.name: scan_url
tools.description: Use this when the person wants a public website checked for security problems, for example "is my site secure?" or "check example.com". Free and read-only: HTTPS, security headers, cookie flags and exposed keys, with a grade from A+ to F and how to fix each finding. Not a pentest. Not for private or local addresses or for code repositories (scan_repo).

url.description: The public address to check, for example https://example.com

language.description: The language the person is writing in, as a BCP 47 tag such as "ru".

tools.name: make_logo
tools.description: Use this when the person wants a new logo, logo options, a brand mark or a brand identity for a business, shop, product or project, whether or not the request names Pugi, for example "make a logo for my bakery" or "make a logo for Blue Fern Bakery". It draws new logos from the interview and takes no uploaded image, so editing or keeping an existing logo file is outside it. A drawn logo changes through refine_logo, its files download from the card when they are ready, and a website can be built from the picked one. Pugi draws up to four whole logo options (PNG) from a short brand interview, the same as on the Pugi logo maker. business_name is the name the person gave, in their own words; with no name given yet, the name comes from the person first (in Russian: «Как называется компания?»), since Pugi draws for a real name only. description and styles are the person's own words about the business and its look; language is the language the person writes in. The first result shows the name in the card for the person to confirm (status needs_input, question id name); each later result is one interview question with its options in the card. An answer comes back with the question_token: trade for the first question, answers for the later ones, draw_now true when the person asks to draw now. The drawing returns state drawing with the question_token and takes about 30 seconds; the same question_token with read_state true returns the finished logos as a replay, with no new charge. A new business name is a new brand. Logos already shown in this conversation change through refine_logo. Generates logo design assets only. Not for photos, illustrations, posters, memes or editing an uploaded image.

business_name.description: The business name, as written by the user.

industry.description: Optional. What the business does, for example "coffee shop" or "accounting firm".

trade.description: The answer to the first interview question (status needs_input): the slug of the option picked, for example "coffee-shop", or the person's own words.

name_proof.description: Set by Pugi's card when the person confirms the name; empty in other calls.

question_token.description: The question_token of the last make_logo result. With the trade, the answers or draw_now it continues that interview; without it a new brief starts.

read_state.description: With question_token: reads what the logo card shows now (the drawn logos with their logo_id, state drawing while they are drawn, or that the person is still answering). A read draws nothing and charges nothing.

answers.description: Every answer so far to the interview questions (status needs_input): the id Pugi gave and the person's own words.

draw_now.description: True when the user wants the logos drawn now, without more questions.

language.description: The language the person writes in, as a BCP 47 tag such as "uk", "de" or "pt-BR"; the questions come back in it.

description.description: The person’s own description of the business, including location, imagery and mood.

colours.description: Optional. Hex colours: {"primary": "#1e3a8a", "secondary": "#f59e0b", "text": "#111827"}, or a list of one to three of them in that order.

style.description: Style words; styles also accepts a list.

idempotency_key.description: A unique string for this call, reused only to retry it. The same key with the same arguments is charged once.

tools.name: publish_status
tools.description: Use this when the person asks which of their Pugi sites are live and at what address.

language.description: The language the person is writing in, as a BCP 47 tag such as "ru".

tools.name: my_sites
tools.description: Use this when the person refers to a site or app they built earlier (in this chat or another one) and its project_id is needed, for example to publish it. It also shows whether a site already exists before a new build. Free and read-only.

tools.name: catalog_search
tools.description: Use this when the person wants ideas or a starting point for a site or app, for example "show me bakery websites". Free. Returns sites and apps people built with Pugi; when none matches it returns the nearest category and says so (match: nearest_category). Each has a brief and the tool that starts a similar project in this chat (build_with). It copies no one's code.

query.description: Optional words for what the person wants, in any language, for example "booking" or "coffee shop".

tags.description: Optional tags; a card matches when it carries every one, for example ["saas"].

limit.description: How many cards to return. Default 10.

tools.name: scan_repo
tools.description: Use this when the person wants a public GitHub repository checked for leaked secrets, vulnerable or malicious dependencies and risky code. No code is run. 3 free checks a day per account, then $1 when the check finishes; a failed check costs nothing. Not for websites (scan_url) or private repositories.

repo_url.description: A public GitHub repository, for example https://github.com/owner/repo

ref.description: Optional branch name. Default: the repository's default branch.

idempotency_key.description: A unique string naming this check. The same key collects the result or retries the check, and is charged once.

language.description: The language the person is writing in, as a BCP 47 tag such as "ru".

tools.name: build_app
tools.description: Use this when the person wants something people use: upload a photo, generate or transform pictures with AI, accounts or sign-in, saved data, a tool, a calculator, a game, bookings, a dashboard. It builds an app, not a landing page. An app that makes pictures with AI asks for the owner's own image-AI key and shows no fake results. brief is the customer's request in the customer's own words, with only the features they asked for (no sign-up, accounts, subscriptions or payments they did not name). When it is built Pugi checks it for security issues, and publish waits for that check. An app that needs a server or a database moves onto Pugi's servers on its own; the person stays in this chat. In hosts that render the build card (MCP Apps or ChatGPT widget) the card tracks progress; in hosts without one (Claude Code or API) job_status reports it until the job is finished, stopped or failed. A simple website is build_site; changes to an app built here go through edit.

without_logo.description: True only when the person said this site should not use the logo they picked.

brief_version.description: With brief_confirmed: the version of the summary the person agreed to, as returned with that summary.

brief_confirmed.description: True only after the person has seen the summary and agreed. In a chat, without it nothing starts and the summary comes back.

site_language.description: Language for the app content; independent of the chat card language.

brief.description: The app to build, in the customer's own words.

max_usd.description: The most this build may cost in USD (default 5).

idempotency_key.description: A unique string naming this build. Reuse it only to retry the same call; it is never charged twice.

language.description: The language the person is writing in, as a BCP 47 tag such as "ru".

tools.name: build_site
tools.description: Use this when the person wants a marketing website for a business, for example "a site for my bakery". Something people use (upload a photo, AI pictures, sign-in, a tool, a game) is an app, made with build_app. brief is the customer's request in the customer's own words, with only the features they asked for (no sign-up, accounts, subscriptions or payments they did not name). The first call starts nothing and returns a summary; its action.arguments start the build once the person agrees. In hosts that render the build card (MCP Apps or ChatGPT widget) the card tracks progress; in hosts without one (Claude Code or API) job_status reports it until the job is finished, stopped or failed. Changes to a built site go through edit.

without_logo.description: True only when the person said this site should not use the logo they picked.

as_site.description: True only when Pugi said this sounds like an app (app_suggested) and the person chose a marketing website anyway.

brief_version.description: With brief_confirmed: the version of the summary the person agreed to, as returned with that summary.

brief_confirmed.description: True only after the person has seen the summary and agreed. In a chat, without it nothing starts and the summary comes back.

site_language.description: Language for the website content; independent of the chat card language.

brief.description: The customer's request in their own words: what the site is for and any pages, texts, colours or style they named, with only the features they asked for.

max_usd.description: The run ceiling in USD; plan builds are included in the subscription. For credit builds, the most this build may cost. Default 5. Credit accounts pay actual cost, usually less.

idempotency_key.description: A unique string naming this job. The same key returns the same job and is never charged twice.

language.description: The language the person is writing in, as a BCP 47 tag such as "ru".

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Use this when the person asks to change a Pugi website or app from this conversation: "change the headline", "make the buttons green", "add a menu page". instruction is the change in the customer's own words, with only what they asked for. job_id or project_id comes from the last build result. It starts no new site or app. In hosts that render the build card (MCP Apps or ChatGPT widget) the card tracks progress; in hosts without one (Claude Code or API) job_status reports it until the job is finished, stopped or failed.

without_logo.description: True only when the person said this site should not use the logo they picked.

brief_version.description: With brief_confirmed: the version of the summary the person agreed to, as returned with that summary.

brief_confirmed.description: True only after the person has seen the summary and agreed. In a chat, without it nothing starts and the summary comes back.

site_language.description: Language for the website content; independent of the chat card language.

job_id.description: The job_id of the build (or of an earlier edit) of the site to change.

project_id.description: Or the project_id of that site.

instruction.description: The change to make, in plain words.

max_usd.description: The run ceiling in USD; plan edits are included in the subscription. For credit edits, the most this change may cost. Default 2.

idempotency_key.description: A unique string naming this job. The same key returns the same job and is never charged twice.

language.description: The language the person is writing in, as a BCP 47 tag such as "ru".

tools.name: job_status
tools.description: Use this when the person asks how a Pugi build or change is going, or for a fresh preview link. In hosts that render the build card (MCP Apps or ChatGPT widget) the card tracks progress; in hosts without one (Claude Code or API) job_status reports it until the job is finished, stopped or failed. Preview links expire after 15 minutes; a new call returns a fresh link.

job_id.description: The job_id build_site, build_app or edit returned.

tools.name: publish
tools.description: Use this when the person asks to put a Pugi website or app live ("publish", "go live"). Free. Puts the latest version on its pugi.app address after the security check every Pugi publish runs; publishing again replaces the live version.

job_id.description: The job_id of the build (or the latest edit) to publish.

project_id.description: Or the project_id of that site.

publish_with_samples.description: Only after the person saw the list of sample details this tool answered with (sample_facts_remain) and chose to keep them.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Reuse it to retry the same publish.

language.description: The language the person is writing in, as a BCP 47 tag such as "ru".

tools.name: select_logo
tools.description: Use this when the person picks one of the Pugi logos shown in this conversation (in the card or in words, such as "the second one"). Saves that logo for their business and returns the summary a website or app will be built from, shown in the card. A change to that summary goes in correction. Draws and buys nothing.

logo_id.description: The logo_id of the picked logo, from the last logo result.

correction.description: The person's correction to the summary, in their own words.

tools.name: refine_logo
tools.description: Use this when the person wants Pugi logos already shown in this conversation changed or redone: other colours (named or hex, for example "dark blue and mint, #112A46 and #14B8A6"), a calmer or bolder mood, another icon or font, "like the second one but blue". Works on the latest set, picked or not. Draws up to four new options from the same brief with that change, with no questions; it does not edit one chosen design. The set is named by one of logo_id (from a logo result) or question_token (from the logo card). A different business name is a new brand (make_logo).

logo_id.description: One logo_id of the set to change, from a logo result (the picked one when there is one); the alternative to question_token.

question_token.description: The question_token of the logo card; the alternative to logo_id.

change.description: The change in the person's own words, for example "make it blue and calmer" or "dark blue and mint (#112A46, #14B8A6)".

language.description: The language the person writes in, as a BCP 47 tag such as "ru".

idempotency_key.description: A unique string for this call, reused only to retry it.

tools.name: open_project
tools.description: Use this when the person wants to open, see or work on one of their Pugi sites or apps in Pugi itself (the full workspace: chat, live preview, files, publish, domain). Pass the project_id from a build or my_sites; without one it opens their newest project. Read-only: it builds, publishes and changes nothing.

project_id.description: The project to open, from a build or my_sites. Optional: the newest project when left out.

language.description: The language the person is writing in, as a BCP 47 tag such as "ru".
